title: Operationalizing Safety Objectives: A Structured Comparison of How Labs Define 'Safe'

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: directly addresses a core open problem. Comparing operationalization depth across labs reveals which approaches are working and where the gap is largest, informing both governance and technical safety efforts.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: coding governance documents against a rubric for operationalization depth is accessible. CS students can apply well-defined criteria (measurable? how measured? internal or external?) to structured documents.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: 10-12 labs, collect safety objectives, code each on three dimensions, compute depth score per lab. Clear enumerated methodology.

novelty.reasoning: The FLI AI Safety Index evaluates labs on safety practices across multiple domains. METR's 'Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies' (2025) identifies shared and divergent elements across frontier safety policies. LessWrong's 'All the labs AI safety plans: 2025 edition' compiles and compares them. Labs are beginning to use capability thresholds (bio, cyber, autonomy) as operationalized safety objectives, with KRIs and KCIs. However, no study uses a structured rubric to score operationalization depth (measurable? how measured? internal/external?) per lab and per safety objective. The specific coding methodology and depth-scoring rubric is a partially novel contribution.
